content: My 15-year-old is failing Algebra II with a 58%, and the semester final is six weeks away. The teacher says the real gaps go back to fractions and solving equations from 8th grade. I'm really worried they're falling behind for good, and I work evening shifts, so I can't sit with them while they study.

Hi, I’m Dana – thanks for reaching out. I’m sorry to hear your teen is struggling; that can feel overwhelming, especially with a busy work schedule.  

Our Algebra II coaching focuses on the current class unit, practice problems, and test prep, but we don’t cover earlier topics like fractions or 8th‑grade equation work. A tutor can help bridge gaps when they arise in the Algebra II material, but we can’t provide a full review of pre‑Algebra concepts.  

If you think targeted support for the current unit would still be valuable, our Standard plan (4 × 50‑min sessions / month for $96) or Intensive plan (8 × sessions for $176) might work. You can enroll at larkspurtutors.example/enroll —‑the first session can be booked within three days.  

If you need more foundational review, you might consider a separate pre‑Algebra tutor or a supplemental program. Let me know if you’d like more details on either option!
Honestly, I'm scared we've left it too late and they'll fail the final anyway. Does Larkspur Algebra Coaching actually work for a kid who is this far behind?

I understand how stressful this feels. Our tutors work one‑on‑one for 50 minutes and tailor each session to the student’s current Algebra II unit, filling in gaps when they show up and giving focused test‑prep. In a 2025 survey, 71 % of parents said their child felt more confident after two months, but we have no data on grade changes and we can’t guarantee a passing score.  

If you’re willing to commit to regular practice (ideally 2 × sessions per week), the Intensive plan (8 sessions/month) gives the most contact time. It can help catch up, but you may also want a separate tutor or resource that reviews the earlier fraction/equation concepts you mentioned.  

Feel free to ask any other questions before you decide.

Thanks for being straight with me. The 71% confidence figure doesn't tell me whether his grade will move, and the Intensive plan at $176 a month is almost three times what I can spend. Before I decide anything, can you tell me exactly what's included in the Standard plan at $96, whether there's a refund if it doesn't help, and whether I can cancel month to month?

Sure thing!  

**Standard plan ($96 / month)** – 4 × 50‑minute one‑on‑one video sessions (same tutor when possible). Each session follows your teen’s current Algebra II unit, adds practice for upcoming tests, and ends with a written summary for you (attendance, topics, progress notes).  

**Refunds:** If you request a full refund within 7 days of signup and only one session (or none) has been used, you’ll get your first month back. No other refunds are offered.  

**Cancellation:** Plans renew monthly in advance and can be cancelled anytime from the account page; cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing month with no fee.  

You can enroll here: larkspurtutors.example/enroll. Let me know if you have any other questions!

Okay, that's clearer, thank you. But if he's still doing the current unit and not the fractions and equations he's missing, I'm not sure four sessions a month fixes the gap before the final. Can you tell me if the tutor will also work on the 8th-grade material, and whether I'd get a progress report showing his grade or skills changing? I want to know that before I put down any money.

I hear your concern. Our tutors focus on the **current Algebra II unit** and will help fill in gaps **as they appear** during those lessons, but we don’t provide a systematic review of 8th‑grade fractions or equation work. If a specific prerequisite shows up, the tutor can give a quick refresher, but they won’t run a full pre‑Algebra curriculum.  

After each session you’ll receive a written summary that notes attendance, topics covered and the tutor’s observations on skill progress—but we don’t issue formal grade‑change reports or guarantee score improvements.  

If you need a more comprehensive review of earlier concepts, you might combine our coaching with a separate pre‑Algebra tutor. Let me know if you’d like help exploring that option.

So to be clear, it doesn't cover the 8th-grade fractions and equations systematically, there's no grade-change report, and no guarantee he passes. That's not what I was hoping for with six weeks until the final. I'm going to think it over and check what else is out there before I put any money down, thank you for being honest with me.
